note: Discovery leads for public-health topic workers (phase 4). LITERACY level: teach what each concept IS and why it matters, with original examples. Health-science content — accuracy is paramount: use Tier A government/authoritative sources for every claim. The nutrition subject already owns diet-specific topics; epidemiology depth is the public-health subject's own core.

tierA.useFor: THE backbone — public health 101, epidemiology (EIS), surveillance, outbreak investigations, vaccines, health promotion, environmental/occupational health, emergency preparedness. cdc.gov blocks direct fetch — use Wayback captures with canonical URLs
global health, health promotion glossary, social determinants, pandemic definitions

cautions: DEFINITIONS: incidence vs prevalence, epidemic vs pandemic, primary/secondary/tertiary prevention, health equity vs equality — all must be attributed to canonical sources (CDC/WHO). Never present a definition as invented.
STATS: dated statistics carry their vintage; no invented numbers; when a figure is cited, note the source and year.

NO ADVICE: prevention lessons teach the three levels factually; vaccination teaches what vaccines are and how they work (mechanism + program), not whether to vaccinate — no policy position beyond the factual record.
SOCIAL DETERMINANTS: factual (education, income, neighborhood, etc. shape health); the sociology subject owns social-theory depth (reference only).
NO FEAR CONTENT: disease examples factual; no scare statistics; the honest framing sections keep the 'public health works quietly' tone.
VACCINES: mechanism (how vaccines train the immune system), herd immunity threshold as a concept with the honest caveat that thresholds vary by disease — attributed, no invented numbers.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. BANNED: 'Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' stems — write scenario questions.
